A working archive · MCDXIV

The records of Vael Anore, kept by hand.

A standing archive of the coastal citadel: tide tallies, oath ledgers, relic witnesses, and the slow correspondence of the inner circle. We do not transcribe by machine. We transcribe by hand, on pressed vellum, and we sign every page.

Plate XXI · Astrolabe reliquary, the sealed customs letter of 1414

Three entries from the chronicle.

Filed in vellum · one volume per reign · signed at the close of every page.

XII · Mar MCDXIV

The Road of No Banners

A lone oath can outlive a kingdom when it is carried without heralds, songs, or witnesses. We hold three such oaths in the cabinet, and we have never opened them; the seal is the signature.

"Signed, sealed, and not opened since the year it was made."
IV · Aug MCDXII

Ash Over Blackstone Gate

When the beacon turned red, the gatehouse learned the old lesson. Stone remembers fire. We entered the ash the morning after, weighed the silver, and recorded the rest in a column marked only with the day's numeral.

XXIX · Oct MCDX

The Last Bell at Dawn

No minstrel sang for the rearguard, but every child inside the walls woke alive. The bell-tower ledger for that quarter has a single entry, written larger than the rest. The entry does not name the rearguard. It names the children.

The relic vault.

Each piece is a sealed witness from a border, a chapel, a battle, or a name that nearly vanished.

Three orders carry the realm.

Not modern features · sworn duties, hard rules, and crafts that keep the citadel breathing.

Order I

The Iron Vow

Sworn defenders

For knights who hold the line when the banners fall and the only command left is duty. The oath is signed in their own blood, then again in ours.

Read the oath
Order II

The Ember Watch

Beacon keepers

Beacon keepers read smoke, weather, and fear before the enemy reaches the valley road. They retire at fifty. They are remembered by name.

Read the watch
Order III

The Scribe's Seal

Court recorders

Every pardon, levy, treaty, and secret sentence is weighed in ink before steel moves. The seal is the second signature, and the only one that travels.

Read the seal

The inner circle.

A throne is only as steady as the hands around it · these are the names trusted with the keys, the maps, and the last words.

Marshal of Roads

Alexander Ashborne

Moves armies by bridges, grain, and timing before a sword leaves its scabbard.

Voice of the Court

Aleks The Gold-Tongued

Turns rival houses into temporary allies when war would cost too much blood.

Silent Captain

Ser Rowan Vale

Commands the final watch. Asks for no song when the torches burn low.

The guild trades.

The realm runs on quiet labor · decrees copied clean, steel kept sharp, roads mapped, promises collected before sunset.
